title: 双日執行役員「豪州投資、リスク低い」
extracted_text:
双日 （2768）がオーストラリアへの成長投資を進めている。2025年6月には豪州インフラ開発会社のカペラ・キャピタルを約4.7億豪ドル（約450億円）で買収した。単一事業への投資として双日では過去最大級だ。カペラを通じたインフラ開発には今後3年間で1000億円程度を投じる計画で、出資案件が相次いだ25年3月期の双日全体の投資規模にのぼる。豪州戦略について、エネルギー・ヘルスケア本部長の西川健史執行役員に聞いた。

――豪州で大型投資が続いています。投資環境は。

「全体として日本との関係がよく、カントリーリスクも低いため、ビジネスが見通しやすい。エネルギー分野では、液化天然ガス（LNG）開発と発電・省エネ事業に主に取り組んでいる。資源大国であると同時に、一人あたりのエネルギー消費量が日本の2倍近くあり足元の脱炭素の流れの中で省エネ事業の成長性が大きい」

「インフラ開発は（公共事業に民間の資本やノウハウを取り入れる）官民パートナーシップ（PPP）の制度が整っている。東南アジアなどでは政府が民間に放り投げるような案件も多い中で、豪州は州政府が市場や民間の声を聞き、許認可の取得や調整のリーダーシップも強い。プロジェクトのしやすさは段違いだ」

――今後、豪州への投資方針は。

「インフラ開発ではカペラを通じて病院や地下鉄など4案件に投資して開発を進めている。（ニュージーランドなどの案件も含め）今後3年ほどで1000億円規模の投資を検討している。開発後の資産入れ替えによるキャッシュも活用すれば、受注できる金額はさらに大きくなる。送電・蓄電設備の開発案件では3件ほど、出資想定額で総額900億円規模の入札に参加しているほか、（32年の）ブリスベン五輪に向けたアリーナ建設の入札にも参加予定だ」

「PPPでは20〜30年単位で期待する利益も含めた投資回収ができるのが一般的だ。開発開始から5年程度で安定稼働するようになれば、毎年一定の金額が政府から入ってくる契約になっている。そうなれば、ファンドなどに資産を売却しエグジット（投資回収）していく。キャッシュフローがほぼ見えているので、資産の買い手も多い」

――エネルギー・ヘルスケア本部として、30年ごろの純利益を26年3月期見通しの300億円から7割増の500億円にする目標を掲げています。どう伸ばしますか。

「米国も含めた再生エネルギーや省エネ事業を現状の約100億円から200億円に伸ばす。カペラを主軸とするインフラ開発で100億円を稼ぐ」

「エネルギーでは既存事業を伸ばしながら、関連する分野への新規投資も行う。例えば、米国では空調事業の会社と電気工事の会社を買収し、顧客に一緒にサービス提供している」

「部門の投下資本キャッシュフロー率（CROIC）は6%（25年3月期2.3%）を目指している。発電事業など極端にCROICの水準が低い事業のエグジットを進めながら、カペラや省エネなど効率の高い事業の比率を増やしていく。カペラではCROIC10%超を狙え、省エネでも十数%ある事業が出てきている」

株価は3月に上場来高値の7257円をつけた。27年3月期までの3カ年の中期経営計画の下、非資源分野を中心に大型投資を積み重ね、成長絵図を描きやすくなったことが市場の評価につながっている。会社計画の26年3月期の連結純利益（国際会計基準）は前期比4%増の1150億円を見込む。

豪州ではインフラ開発のほか、出資するレアアース同国最大手のライナスを通じて、日本企業として初めて中国外から希少性の高い重希土類を調達した。ライナスと共同で豪州内外での新規鉱山開発に乗り出すことも発表した。

ただ、豪州では中古車販売事業と原料炭事業で赤字から抜け出せずにいる。植村幸祐社長は「売却や撤退などの選択肢も含めて判断していく」と方針を示している。

（佐藤優衣）

［デジタル版・日経ヴェリタス2026年3月25日公開　ここが知りたいを一部要約］

translated_text:
Sojitz (2768) is pursuing growth investment in Australia. In June 2025, the company acquired Australian infrastructure developer Capela Capital for approximately 470 million Australian dollars (about 45 billion yen). This represents Sojitz's largest single-project investment to date. Through Capela, the company plans to invest approximately 100 billion yen in infrastructure development over the next three years, matching the total investment scale for the entire fiscal year ended March 2025. We spoke with Kenji Nishikawa, Executive Officer and Head of the Energy and Healthcare Division, about the Australia strategy.

-- You have been making large investments in Australia. How is the investment environment?

"Overall, relations with Japan are good, and country risk is low, making business outlook clear. In the energy sector, we are primarily focused on liquefied natural gas (LNG) development and power generation and energy conservation projects. Australia is a major resource country, and with per-capita energy consumption nearly twice that of Japan, there is significant growth potential for energy conservation businesses amid the current decarbonization trend."

"Infrastructure development benefits from a well-established public-private partnership (PPP) system that incorporates private capital and expertise into public projects. In Southeast Asia, many projects are simply handed off to the private sector by governments, but in Australia, state governments listen to market and private-sector voices, and take strong leadership in obtaining permits and coordination. The ease of proceeding with projects is far superior."

-- What is your future investment policy toward Australia?

"In infrastructure development, we are investing through Capela in four projects including hospitals and subway lines. (Including projects in New Zealand and elsewhere), we are considering investments of approximately 100 billion yen over the next three years. By utilizing cash from asset replacement after development, the contract amounts we can secure will be even larger. In power transmission and storage facility development, we are participating in bids for about three projects with a combined assumed investment amount of 90 billion yen, and we also plan to participate in bids for arena construction ahead of the 2032 Brisbane Olympics."

"In PPP, it is common to recover investments over a 20-30 year period while including expected profits. If operations stabilize around five years after development begins, there are contracts in place for fixed annual payments from the government. Once that happens, we can sell assets to funds and exit the investment. Since the cash flow is almost clear, there are many buyers for such assets."

-- As the Energy and Healthcare Division, you have set a target of increasing net income by 70% to 50 billion yen by the 2030s, up from the 26 billion yen forecast for the fiscal year ending March 2026. How will you achieve this growth?

"We will expand our renewable energy and energy conservation business, including in the US, from the current approximately 10 billion yen to 20 billion yen. We will generate 10 billion yen in profits from infrastructure development with Capela as the core."

"In energy, while expanding existing businesses, we will also make new investments in related fields. For example, in the US, we acquired an air-conditioning company and an electrical engineering company to provide integrated services to customers."

"Our division's Cash Return on Invested Capital (CROIC) target is 6% (up from 2.3% for the fiscal year ended March 2025). While proceeding with exit strategies for businesses with extremely low CROIC such as power generation, we will increase the ratio of more efficient businesses like Capela and energy conservation. Capela aims for CROIC above 10%, and some energy conservation businesses are already generating returns in the teens."

The stock price hit a record high of 7,257 yen in March. Under the three-year medium-term business plan through March 2027, the company has been accumulating large investments primarily in non-resource businesses, making it easier to绘制 a growth roadmap, which has earned market approval. The company forecasts consolidated net income (under international accounting standards) for the fiscal year ending March 2026 of 115 billion yen, representing a 4% increase from the previous year.

In addition to infrastructure development in Australia, through Lynas, the largest rare earth company in the country in which Sojitz invests, the company became the first Japanese company to procure high-priority heavy rare earth elements from outside China. It was also announced that Lynas and Sojitz will jointly launch new mining development projects in Australia and overseas.

However, in Australia, the company remains unprofitable in its used car sales and thermal coal businesses. President Yukisuke Uemura indicated that the company will make decisions including considering options such as sale or withdrawal.

(Sato Yui)

[Excerpted from Nikkei Veritas digital edition, published March 25, 2026]
